name: Missing Synchronization
principle: Code uses a shared resource concurrently without any synchronization. Unsynchronized access can expose stale, interleaved, or inconsistent state and can let attacker-influenced timing alter data or execution logic.
detection_signals: pthread_create or std::thread or ExecutorService with shared mutable variable access and no pthread_mutex_lock/std::mutex/synchronized/ReentrantLock
global/static mutable variable read and written by multiple threads without atomic type or lock guard
shared FILE*/stdout/file descriptor written by forked processes or threads using putc/write/fflush with no flockfile/flock/fcntl lock
Java static mutable field updated outside synchronized method/block and not Atomic*
check-then-act on shared Map/List/cache such as containsKey()+put() or size()+get() with no lock
lazy singleton pattern if (instance == null) instance = new X() without synchronized, Lock, or volatile double-checking
negative_signals: every access to the shared resource is inside the same pthread_mutex_lock/unlock, synchronized(lock), or ReentrantLock lock/finally unlock
C++ access protected by std::lock_guard, std::unique_lock, or std::scoped_lock using the same mutex
shared counter/state implemented with std::atomic or Java AtomicInteger/AtomicReference atomic operations
state is immutable after construction using final/const and is only read concurrently
data is thread-local, stack-local, or passed by value with no shared mutable alias
ConcurrentHashMap or other concurrent collection uses atomic APIs such as computeIfAbsent, putIfAbsent, or compute
false_defense_traps: volatile alone used for compound operations such as ++, check-then-act, or lazy initialization
only writes are locked while reads of the same shared state are unlocked
different locks protect the same resource in different methods
Collections.synchronizedMap used but iteration occurs outside synchronized(map)
double-checked locking without volatile on the shared instance field
verification_focus: Is every concurrent access to the same mutable resource protected by one consistent synchronization mechanism or atomic operation?

consequence_chains.trigger: two threads or processes access the same mutable resource and at least one writes without synchronization
consequence_chains.consequence: race condition causing corrupted data, stale reads, or altered execution logic

consequence_chains.trigger: unsynchronized read observes partially updated or unintended shared state
consequence_chains.consequence: confidential application data can be exposed

patch_principle: Identify all shared mutable resources and all threads/processes that access them.
Guard every read and write with the same mutex, monitor, file lock, or lock object.
Use atomic types or concurrent collections for simple shared state and atomic compound operations.
Avoid shared mutable state by using immutable objects, thread-local storage, message passing, or joining before shared output.
Document lock ownership and keep lock/unlock in finally/RAII to prevent missed release paths.

minimal_examples.vuln: counter++; // shared static/global counter used by multiple threads
